title: CORS Misconfiguration on api.monzo.com and internal-api.monzo.com reflects arbitrary Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

evidence.description: Both api.monzo.com and internal-api.monzo.com reflect any arbitrary Origin header in Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header while simultaneously setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. No Vary: Origin header is present. This applies to all tested endpoints including authenticated ones (/accounts returns 401 with reflected CORS, /balance returns 400 with reflected CORS). Null origin is also reflected.

infrastructure.host_header_reflection: Root endpoint reflects Host header value into JSON body

exploitability_assessment.attack_scenario: Attacker-controlled website can make credentialed cross-origin requests to api.monzo.com. If a victim visits the attacker site while logged into Monzo, the browser will send session cookies due to ACAC:true. The reflected ACAO allows the attacker JS to read responses from authenticated endpoints that return user data.
limitations: Exploitability depends on whether api.monzo.com uses cookie-based auth vs Bearer tokens only
OAuth public client credentials in env.js are explicitly out of scope per Monzo comments
Need to verify if any authenticated GET endpoint returns PII/financial data accessible via browser session
exploitability_assessment.false_positive_risk: Medium - Monzo may use token-only auth making cookie-based CORS exploitation non-viable

next_steps: Check Intigriti portal for existing CORS reports on Monzo
Verify authentication mechanism (cookie vs bearer-only) on api.monzo.com
If exploitable, draft report with PoC HTML page
dedup_notes: Intigriti Researcher API v1 has no submission/search endpoint. Portal login required for manual dedup but credentials not available in headless session.
exploitability_rationale: CORS misconfiguration confirmed on internal-api.monzo.com (reflects arbitrary Origin + ACAC:true). However: (1) api.monzo.com does NOT reflect CORS headers at all (Cloudflare strips or never sets them). (2) internal-api.monzo.com sets NO cookies whatsoever - not even __cf_bm. (3) auth.monzo.com only sets __monzo_locale_v1__ (preference) and __cf_bm (bot management), neither is a session cookie. (4) Monzo API uses OAuth2 Bearer tokens per public docs; browsers do not send Authorization headers cross-origin even with credentials:true. (5) Without cookie-based session auth on the vulnerable host, cross-origin credentialed requests cannot exfiltrate user data. Finding is technically valid CORS misconfiguration but lacks exploitability path for data theft.
recommendation: DO_NOT_SUBMIT unless cookie-based auth discovered. Misconfiguration is real but not exploitable for account takeover or data exfiltration under current auth model. Monitor for changes to session handling.
